title: Canonical projection and exchange maps on internal pro-etale modules
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $R_Z=\Lambda_Z$ its pullback to the small pro-etale site of a scheme $Z$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $D(Z)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_Z})$ for the ordinary unbounded internal-module derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] with its relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Use the canonical derived adjunctions $F_h=h^*\dashv R_h=Rh_*$ [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction]. The canonical tensor comparison $\mu_h:F_h(A\otimes B)\simeq F_hA\otimes F_hB$ is the representative-normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], in the existing internal-module interface [def-sfb-proetale-rational-localizing-projection-helpers]. Define the left-factor projection $\pi_{h,K,N}:K\otimes R_hN\to R_h(F_hK\otimes N)$ as the counit mate of $1\otimes\varepsilon_N$, using $\mu_h$; equivalently conjugate the right-factor projection mate by the canonical Koszul braidings. For scheme maps $f:X\to Y$, $p_1,p_2:W\to X$ and a commuting square $fp_1=fp_2$, let $c:F_{p_2}F_f\simeq F_{p_1}F_f$ be the canonical pullback-composition comparison through $F_{fp_2}=F_{fp_1}$. Define $b_2:F_fR_f\to R_{p_2}F_{p_1}$ to be the mate of $c$ under the two specified derived adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; swapping the projections gives $b_1$. These are actual maps, with no invertibility hypothesis or arbitrary map parameters. The functor aliases $F_h,R_h$ are the existing `tracePull` and `tracePush` declarations exported by [def-sfb-proetale-trace-coefficient-interfaces]; they are reused, not declared again.
